questions.question: How should glob handle a pattern with a leading `/` (BK-405's open decision)? Today the answer depends on root_path.

options.label: Refuse under any root (Recommended)
options.description: Amend GLOB-007 so Store.glob and the fallback raise InvalidPath for `/d/*.csv` under any root_path. The answer stops depending on configuration, matching how the kernel refuses an absolute-looking key. Behavior change: a non-empty-root GLOB store that matched today will raise.

options.label: Strip under any root
options.description: Amend GLOB-007 to drop the leading `/` everywhere. More lenient and the same under every root, but it silently accepts a spelling the kernel's key rule refuses for keys.

options.label: Refuse in fallback only
options.description: No GLOB-007 change: the fallback refuses, so it agrees with the GLOB tier only under an empty root. Smallest diff, but the dependence on root_path remains.

questions.question: How should BUG-298 be fixed (`*.csv` matching `a.csv\n`)?

options.label: Anchor with \Z everywhere (Recommended)
options.description: pattern_to_regex ends with \Z, so SQLBlob, ext.glob, S3 and Azure (async too) all stop matching. Add a conformance cell for a key ending in a newline. One shared fix with a precise rule.

options.label: Document it in GLOB-014
options.description: Keep `$` and state in the spec that a single trailing newline is ignored. No code change, but it makes a surprising result official.

options.label: Leave it

questions.question: Should a glob pattern go through spec 004's input normalization before matching, so `/d/*.csv`, `./d/*.csv` and `d//*.csv` all mean the Key pattern `d/*.csv` under every root?

options.label: Normalize like a path (Recommended)
options.description: Amend GLOB-007: Store.glob and the ext.glob fallback strip a leading `/` and drop `//` and `.` segments, refuse `..`, and keep a trailing `/`. Glob then matches read/exists/list_files (PATH-004/005) and TREE-011, and the GLOB and fallback paths agree under any root. Behavior change: Local with an empty root returns matches instead of raising NotImplementedError.

options.label: Refuse under any root
options.description: InvalidPath for a leading `/` in glob only. Root-independent, but glob becomes the one Store method that rejects a spelling read/exists/list_files accept.

The new conformance test (newline key) fails on Windows: Local cannot create `b.csv\n`, and LocalBackend.write leaks a raw OSError (Errno 22), an untracked Local bug. How should this PR get green?

options.label: Drop cell, file Local bug (Recommended)
options.description: Remove the new conformance test from this PR and file a BUG for Local's raw OSError on Windows, with this CI log as the reproduction. BUG-298 stays covered: regex unit tests, SQLBlob's real SQL path, and the Memory fallback. The cell returns when a kernel GLOB driver lands (BK-446). PR scope stays glob-only.

options.label: Map the error in Local
options.description: Fix LocalBackend.write in this PR (EINVAL → InvalidPath), so the existing skip applies. That widens the PR into Local error mapping, which can only be verified on Windows CI (none here), and other write paths (write_atomic, move, copy) would then be inconsistent.

options.label: Skip on OSError too
options.description: Widen the test's skip to also catch OSError. Smallest diff, but the skip would then hide the very error-mapping bug the test just found.
